articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully lifts off to explore Phobos, marking an ambitious journey to Mars's enigmatic moon.

articles.title: NASA adopting Apollo's urgency to build a moon base and land astronauts within 2 years
articles.description: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA is accelerating its Artemis program to establish a lunar base and return astronauts to the Moon within two years. This ambitious timeline reflects renewed momentum in human space exploration.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered an extraordinary system of three actively feeding black holes within a single galaxy from over 12.5 billion light-years away. This remarkable find challenges theories about early universe black hole formation.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified evidence of what may be the first moon ever detected orbiting an exoplanet beyond our Solar System. This historic discovery opens new frontiers in understanding planetary systems.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu mission contain 4.5-billion-year-old material revealing new secrets about Solar System formation. This breakthrough evidence rewrites our understanding of planetary origins.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: Analysis of nearly 3,000 exploding stars provides new evidence supporting dark energy theories and advancing our understanding of cosmic expansion. This massive dataset significantly strengthens cosmological models.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.description: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured humanity's first photograph of Earth from space, a landmark achievement that pioneered the space age and transformed our perspective.

articles.title: NASA adopting Apollo’s urgency to build a moon base and land astronauts within two years
articles.description: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.
articles.summary: NASA is accelerating plans to establish a moon base and land astronauts within two years, demonstrating renewed urgency for lunar exploration.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: Astronomers observe stellar formation occurring within a nebula, revealing the dynamic processes that birth new stars in cosmic nurseries.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates its eight-year anniversary milestone in its groundbreaking mission to explore Mercury's mysteries and physics.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope discovers a previously unknown comet, demonstrating the ongoing capacity to uncover new celestial visitors.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The MMX mission is set to launch on the H3 rocket, beginning its historic expedition to explore the Martian moons.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: Solar Orbiter traces the origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks in solar wind, advancing understanding of solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: 27 Exoplanet Targets for the World's First Private Space Telescope
articles.description: Get ready for the age of private space telescopes. The Lazuli Space Telescope will launch in a few years and part of its mission is to observe exoplanets. New research presents a list of 27 exoplanet targets, some of which are very well-known and will certainly benefit from deeper observations.
articles.summary: The Lazuli Space Telescope will soon pioneer private space telescope exploration, targeting 27 exoplanets and ushering in a new era of discovery.

articles.title: The Largest Canyon in the Solar System is Still Tectonically Active
articles.description: Scientists at Imperial College London and Columbia University have found that the largest canyon system in the solar system is still active and shaping Mars today, billions of years after it first formed.
articles.summary: Valles Marineris, the solar system's largest canyon, continues to exhibit active tectonic processes, revealing ongoing geological evolution on Mars.

articles.title: JWST Reveals a Lopsided Alien World with Blistering Evening Winds
articles.description: Typically, when we think of exoplanets, we think of neat spheres floating directly in front of their star, which acts as a giant spotlight. From our vantage point, they would look more like two perfect two dimensional circles than spheres, though. But nature is almost never so clean-cut. A new paper published in Nature Astronomy from researchers at Cornell and the University of Bristol details the first-ever study of an exoplanet that is noticeably lopsided.
articles.summary: JWST reveals a surprisingly asymmetrical exoplanet with extreme blistering evening winds, challenging conventional models of planetary atmospheres.

articles.title: Advancing Astronomy at MIT with X-ray Reverberation Mapping
articles.description: Professor Erin Kara of MIT's Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research is helping advance our understanding of the most extreme objects in the Universe by analyzing X-ray reverberations and other astrophysical data.
articles.summary: MIT researchers use X-ray reverberation mapping to advance understanding of black hole behavior and accretion processes. This innovative technique provides new insights into some of the universe's most extreme objects.

articles.title: Milky Way's disk grew 'upside down,' with younger stars forming in ever-thinner layers
articles.description: The Milky Way is home to hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a glorious spiral pattern. But beyond the obvious spiral, our galaxy has other physical characteristics. It's divided into a galactic bulge, a galactic disk and a galactic halo.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New research reveals the Milky Way's disk formed in an unexpected 'upside down' pattern with younger stars in progressively thinner layers. This discovery reshapes our understanding of galactic evolution and structure.

articles.title: Everyday Mylar turned into a promising insulator for lunar habitats
articles.description: Establishing a long-term presence on the moon will require solving challenges that are easy to overlook on Earth. Lunar temperatures, for instance, can vary from hundreds of degrees below zero to boiling, making effective insulation essential for lunar habitats.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an innovative insulation material using everyday Mylar for lunar habitats. This breakthrough demonstrates creative problem-solving for sustaining long-term human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Black holes spinning near maximum rate could split in two, calculations suggest
articles.description: Two black holes can collide and merge into one. But could the opposite happen: could a single black hole split into two smaller ones? That question is explored in a new theoretical study: "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," published in the journal Physical Review D.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Theoretical calculations suggest rapidly spinning black holes could potentially split into two separate black holes under certain conditions. This surprising finding challenges conventional black hole physics.

articles.title: ALMA spots 'dragon egg' that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation
articles.description: Astronomers identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent an early stage in the formation of a massive star. Located in an infrared-dark area called Dragon Cloud, the core is nicknamed the "dragon egg." The paper, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 5.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: ALMA telescope observations have identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation. This discovery provides unprecedented insights into stellar birth.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Balloon-borne telescope observations have uncovered a mysterious and complex magnetic web above the Sun's surface. This discovery reveals hidden structure in seemingly calm solar regions.

articles.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
articles.description: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.
articles.summary: Scientists have solved a 178-year-old mystery about a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing new insights into historical space weather events and their effects on Earth.

articles.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
articles.description: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: A study of 13 astronauts reveals that the human heart may be remarkably well-adapted for long-duration spaceflight to Mars, offering promising signs for future crewed missions.

articles.title: NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch?
articles.description: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight, which is scheduled to launch to Earth orbit next year. But a firm liftoff date has not yet been announced.
articles.summary: NASA has revealed comprehensive plans for the Artemis III moon-lander test flight, marking a significant milestone in humanity's return to the lunar surface.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Scientists explore the leading giant impact hypothesis, which proposes that a planet-sized collision with Earth formed our Moon during the early solar system.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL researchers envision ambitious future innovations including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters over the next 90 years of exploration.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar, a significant discovery expanding our understanding of compact celestial objects and their behavior in the universe.

articles.title: What SpaceX Just Revealed About Starship Is Incredible!
articles.description: This video, hosted by Marcus House, covers a packed week of space news with a primary focus on SpaceX's Starship program and other aerospace developments. Starship and SpaceX Updates: Flight 14 Recap: The video highlights Flight 14, noting the successful depl…
articles.summary: Marcus House covers a packed week of space news focusing on SpaceX's Starship program developments and recent achievements.

articles.title: La NASA ha tenuto una conferenza sulle future missioni Artemis III e Artemis IV: queste le novità
articles.description: Nella serata di ieri si è tenuta una conferenza della NASA per riportare gli aggiornamenti delle future missioni Artemis III e Artemis IV. Le novità riguardano le operazioni e i veicoli impiegati con il primo allunaggio previsto per la fine del 2028.
articles.summary: NASA held a conference revealing exciting updates about the upcoming Artemis III and Artemis IV missions to return humans to the Moon.
